Series::topk_pair¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

std::pair<Series, Series> Series::topk_pair(
    std::int64_t k,
    std::int64_t dim = -1,
    bool largest = true,
    bool sorted = true) const

Select Values And Provenance Together¶

topk_pair() selects k entries from every lane of one axis and returns both their values and their local source positions. It is the provenance-preserving selection operation: .first contains values and .second contains int64 indices suitable for gathering aligned data along the same axis.

Unlike a full sort, selection need not establish an order among entries that cannot enter the result. Use it when only an extreme subset matters. Use topk() for values alone and sort_pair() when all entries and their positions are required.

Parameters And Contract¶

Parameter

Meaning

Default

k

Number selected from each lane. Must satisfy 0 <= k <= size(dim).

Required

dim

Selection axis; negative values count from the end.

-1

largest

Select largest values when true, smallest when false.

true

sorted

Put selected values in rank order when true; leave their order unspecified when false.

true

Both outputs have the receiver’s rank. Their extent on dim becomes k; all other extents are unchanged. The value dtype and platform are preserved, and indices are int64 on that platform. k=0 is valid and returns matching empty outputs. A negative or oversized k is an error, not a request to clamp.

Equal boundary values may be represented by any qualifying source position; there is no stability option. When sorted=false, only membership is contractual: consumers must not infer rank from output position.

Reverse Mode And Execution¶

Selection writes values and indices in one kernel. On CPU, sorted=true uses partial ordering rather than sorting the entire lane. sorted=false can use partitioning and may be cheaper. The value output is differentiable and scatters sensitivity to the exact returned positions; indices do not carry sensitivity.

Examples¶

1. Two Largest Values Per Row¶

auto table = pluss::make_series({
    {4.0, 1.0, 4.0, 2.0},
    {3.0, 5.0, 0.0, 5.0},
});
auto result = table.topk_pair(2, 1);
std::cout << "values=" << result.first << "\nindices=" << result.second;

Output¶

values=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[4, 4],
  [5, 5]]
indices=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[2, 0],
  [3, 1]]

Both ties qualify. Their relative order is deliberately unspecified.

2. Select The Smallest Values With A Negative Axis¶

auto result = table.topk_pair(2, -1, false, true);
std::cout << "values=" << result.first << "\nindices=" << result.second;

Output¶

values=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 2],
  [0, 3]]
indices=pluss::Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 3],
  [2, 0]]

3. Request Membership Without Ordering¶

auto x = pluss::make_series({9LL, 1LL, 7LL, 3LL, 5LL});
auto result = x.topk_pair(3, 0, true, false);
std::cout << "values=" << result.first << "\nindices=" << result.second;

Output¶

values=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[9, 7, 5]
indices=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 2, 4]

This run happens to appear ordered; sorted=false does not promise that order, so portable code treats these three entries as an unordered set.

4. Select Nothing Without Special-Case Control Flow¶

auto result = table.topk_pair(0, 1);
std::cout << "values=" << result.first << "\nindices=" << result.second;

Output¶

values=pluss::Series(shape=[2,0], strides=[0,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=0, contiguous=true)
[]
indices=pluss::Series(shape=[2,0], strides=[0,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=0, contiguous=true)
[]

5. Reject An Oversized Selection¶

try { (void)table.topk_pair(5, 1); }
catch (const std::exception& error) {
  std::string message = error.what();
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

topk_pair: k must be <= size(dim)

Invalid axes, negative k, complex ordered input, and undefined receivers are also rejected.
